subject.title: [Bug]: Teams app removal/re-add retains prior DM session history

question: Should OpenClaw reset Microsoft Teams sessions only on bot-visible app/removal lifecycle boundaries, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100371 be the canonical fix over https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100350?
rationale: The choice affects retained personal-chat history, proactive conversation references, and whether OpenClaw documents Teams-local clear history as an unobservable platform limitation rather than a fixed lifecycle boundary.

options.title: Land scoped lifecycle reset
options.body: Review and land the stronger lifecycle/session-reset PR, with explicit documentation that Teams-local clear history without a bot-visible signal is not covered.

options.title: Require broader forget policy
options.body: Pause both PRs until maintainers define a user-facing Teams forget/reset policy for clear-history expectations that Teams does not expose to bots.

options.title: Reject server-side reset
options.body: Close the linked fixes and document Teams app removal as outside OpenClaw's retention boundary unless users explicitly reset sessions.

recommendation.title: Land scoped lifecycle reset
recommendation.body: Review and land the stronger lifecycle/session-reset PR, with explicit documentation that Teams-local clear history without a bot-visible signal is not covered.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent Teams state-store and security-sensitive ownership signal for deciding the retained-history boundary.
